title: 2025 recap
body:
Year of self protection! 

Payoff of the hard work in research from 2024 and trying to figure out what’s next career wise 

started to really trying to process an interpersonally traumatic 2024 and reevaluate why I keep putting ppl above me when they don’t appreciate or really see me, decided to continuously try to protect my energy more and work through my self-sacrificing behavior 

Feeling a better sense of stability and learning to release control/ manage conflict better through my relationship 

January 
- conference in Hawaii! I love the beach I need to settle down near a beach 
- began realizing how my mental health slides when I’m at home
- Still feeling incredibly lonely and recovering from 2024

February
- struggling with feeling a sense of non-belonging n ppl that align w my fundamental morals 
- Trying to depend on my siblings more for support 

March
- had bad habits of overgiving and not realizing it
- Had no life outside of work lol 
- Felt like I was getting trapped in unhealthy dynamics but also didn’t know what to do bc it didn’t seem like I could meet people that would actually vibe with me so I brushed my feelings away and didn’t change my behavior 

April
- Finally got to enjoy nyc after paper submission and run around town 
- Greek Easter
- went to CHI! First paper was a success and felt like my work was paying off 

May
- Continued travelling to Japan with Tao and my sister!! So chill and nice 
- Went to see my grandpa and extended family in China and was emo about being away from them (I promised myself to take advantage of being a student as much as possible and come back often)
- Realized at how bad I am at noticing I something is wrong and how it’s usually too late bc I doubt my intuition

June
- spent the summer in the bay before the phd!
- Went to SD w hs friends!
- Told my advisor I wanted to learn how to develop my own ideas from scratch 
- Realized the depth at which *childhood trauma* is the cause for me to absorb blame and overgive and end up in bad situations 
- Mental health slid after fat triggers 
- First couples trip with Nikos to mammoth lakes where I drove entire time

July 
- decided I need to stand up for myself and actively tried to remove myself from bad situations 
- Went to Tahoe and rafting for July 4th! 
- Had many mental breakdowns reliving past interpersonal conflicts, also trauma dumped it all over nikos lol
- got to hang out w the friends in the bay! And hang out w grandparents and bonded w my grandpa abt research 
- Decided to heavily explore and prioritize hobbies like art, vlogging, painting, music in the future 

August
- went to Greece to meet Nikos family! I have loved Greece ever since 6th grade and now I feel like I manifested it 
- Came back to nyc and had panic attacks of feeling like I couldn’t rely on anyone
- Trying to be intentional of what type of friends I want to make and the type of community I want to build

September 
- met friends who matched my energy better and I didn’t feel like I was over exerting myself into forcing square into a circle
- Started PhD officially and trying to navigate around my advisor lol
- Put way too much pressure on myself and forgot why I liked research to begin with 
- Began doing a lot more self care as a form of self soothing

October 
- Continued to put unnecessary pressure on myself and hold myself to an insane standard work-wise
- Beat myself up over situations bc of self-doubt
- Became too codependent because I was so scared 
- Burnt out like crazy

November
- tried to make mental shift again to spend more time alone
- still doubted myself and my decisions a lot but felt more validated about my gut intuitions (but I shouldn’t have to wait for external validation for me to feel some type of way!)
- Felt more healthy but still prone to panic attacks and not even realizing something is triggering me 
- Relationship with work was changing for the better again although still in the gutter 
- Many double dates!! Happy to find double date situations 

December 
- Validated that the situation I was trying to leave was worth leaving and that I need to trust my intuition 
- Tryna fuckin push thru some panic attacks, learning to regulate by waiting until my heart rate comes down to take my thoughts seriously
- Trying to figure out what’s fair vs not and what i can reasonably expect of myself and others 
- Instinctively operated from a place of scarcity/low self esteem again bc my mental health slides at home lol 
- Went to Taiwan before going back to motherland to hang out w my extended family fam!  

Overall I had to confront of a lot of things with myself this year and shed behavior that was not serving me! Ongoing process :) 

next year I want to manage my anxiety and ocd a lot better and let things go (as a form of taking care of myself) without trying to control the future.  Continuing to be more intentional/practice self care and I start to work through some of my resentments so I can exist with more peace and safety. I want to trust more with people who show me they’ve trust worthy instead of letting the past fuck shit up and build a stronger community and get better at communicating things I dislike

title: Paper
body:
Paper
GENERATIVE DISCO ? ? 

Title
Enforcing Developer Rules with XX 
Ensuring ?  Agents.MD with Rule Enforcement 
Enforcing Agent.MD Rules with ___ 

Enforcing Developer Rules for Vibe-Coding Complex Tasks ?




1 Introduction
Motivation
- LLMs have fundamentally transformed how people code. 
- Developers today embrace vibe-coding, a practice where users iteratively prompt, review, and adapt AI-generated code. 
- Typically developers will have the agent create a super detailed plan and let it code, then come back to it later and test and review the code. 
- A widespread practice in vibe-coding is providing context files like AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md, or .md files in /.rules folders) to guide agent behavior. They have different names -- we will cal all of such files AGENTS.md files for simplification (as it is the industry standard as well). Such context files are included in over 60,000 open source repositories at the time of writing (as reported by Agents.md). 
- They typically contain repository-level and user-level rules to help coding agents behavior align more to the user’s satisfaction. For example, there can be code style rules (“imports at the top of the file”), UI-UX rules (“Use my design system and color scheme instead of that provided by MUI”), data-level rules (“ALWAYS create firebase composite index”), testing rules (“”).
- These rules exist to help the code more efficiently and so the user doesn’t have to babysit or supervise the coding agent. 

Existing solutions attempt to fix these agentic behavior flaws by giving the agents rules, memory, and context [6, 7].  They make shallow clarifying questions even when the system prompts them to think. When faced with complex bugs, they will locally patch symptoms instead of engineering real solutions. These solutions diagnose the right problems, but don’t enforce the behaviors needed to actually solve them.
Problem
- While developers praise the concept of AGENTS.md, in practice, they still fall apart because the rules, memory, and context aren’t enforced in action.
-  For longer vibe-coding sessions where users are making significant changes to complex code-bases of over 10k lines, coding agents are notorious for skipping steps even when they created detailed plans for long tasks. 
- This problem extends to AGENTS.md files.as the session goes on, coding agents can completely disregard the files, hallucinate, and forget that they exist in the first place. Thus, they ignore coding conventions even when the conventions are documented. 
- Second, because oftentimes the coding agent themselves update the AGENT.md files, the context can become bloated or even contradicting. The agent can get confused when generating code. [INSERT EXAMPLE]
- Finally, if the final product is bad, there is no way to verify the agent has followed the AGENTS.md in the middle of the coding session because usually you just let them code and then you don’t know whats happened and then the developer tests it. 
- Different structures have been explored with storing AGENTS.md files, such as putting multiple context files in different folders, which can improve the performance, but the problem still exists Adding more context or aggressive prompting has marginal benefits as well. 
- The fundamental problem is that it is notguaranteed that the agent will follow the AGENTS.md, the context the agent and user have accumulated and learned often go to waste.

Approach
* Systems must actively enforce that coding agents follow the rules in their AGENTS.md files.
* We present Zoro, a rule enforcement system that pairs with coding agents (Claude code, CodeX, Cline, etc.) that ensures rules in AGENTS.md file are retrieved, applied, and validated at each step of the plan. 
* Zoro is meant for long vibe-coding session with a complex or hairy task on complicated codebase. It is not meant for exploration. 
* Zoro ensures that each plan created by a coding agent is enriched by rules and planned down to the rule level. 
* For every step of the plan, each step and each rule must be validated — aka, Then for every step of the plan, each step must validated — aka, all important rules must be EFORCED by an agent checking to see if it exists in the codebase otherwise you can’t move on to the next step, and also the STEP itself must be validated otherwise you can’t move on.
* This prevents the LLM from actively forgetting things, skipping steps, skipping rules, and being overeager.
* Users can see what step is completed, what code snippets are attributed to each step and each rule, and follow along the process and gain trust 

Evaluation 
To understand zoro’s effectiveness, we conducted a XYZ

Contributiosn 
* Enforcement 
* System
* Technical Evaluation 
* User Evaluation 

2 Related Work
Coding agents 

Policies



 

3 Zoro Design and Motivation 

In the first stage of our research we looked at how people vibe-code today and how they use rules files.
There is a rate of people who use it, some use it exentisvely others don’t 
We talked to 3 programmers that vibe-code daily (one start up, one industry, one PhD), and sat them down. and all participants had prior experience in large codebases and commonly code I large codebases with rules files and etc. XY worke dMETRICS

Sat down with 3 of them that use rules file
Talked with 10 programmers 

Sat with 3 of them for  1-2 hours while they vibe-coded to understand their processes and whatnot 

The lead author sat down with each person and asked them some question about vibe-coding a their epxeirnce with rules files. Then watched them complete a task on their codebase vibe-coding .Participants were asked to think outloud. Afterwards we asked on their thoughts and how they typically approach XYZ

We analyzed the sessions following a thematic approach where one did XY

We observed that people’s workflows tend to match this: 
1. Planning 
2. Pass
3. Inspection ?? 
4. Repeat (depending on bugs)

Users plan with AI for undetermined amoutn of time. They are generally pretty detailed and the user likes them. Although it’s hard to know what context the plan in sfactoring in from the AGENTS.md wise.

Then the AI gets a pass. During the first pass, this is where the things kind of go wrong

During the process o the first pass, usually the AI is moving too fast and the user has no clue what is going on

After its done, its unclear what the LLM has built so the user has to Kinda sift through

Only by manually testing stufff can the user figure out whats wrong but its hard to debug bc they didnt code it in the fist place 

u give the AI one pass at doing things and then u fix the errors after and oftentimes it gets stuck in a loop and yeah

Oftentimes they figure out that the LLM has either lied and not completed the full plan (like its done step 1-4 but not up until step 8) and certain rules were not followed.
And hen the user kinda enters this loop with AI where they fight with it 

The rules file becomes bloated and the user themselves is confused what rule to follow or not 

Our study showed the following challenges:

1. Skipping steps
2. Conforming to what the Agent wants because it isn’t following the structure 
3. No real clue what the agent is doing
4. Bloated context files 

This causes the users to conform to them 

Based on our formative study, we derived several motivations for our enforcement system

4 System - User Scenario and Interface Walkthrough
- Based on these motivations, we designed Zoro, and visualization system that also actively enforces the plan and rules given a vibe-coding session.
- It can be used in tandem with any vibe-coding tools, such as claude code, codex, cline, cursor etc.
- Zoro is meant for coding sessions on very large and hairy codebases where code quality and style matter.
- It also supports difficult, multi-step tasks, such as full-stack features, migrations, refactors. 
    - For simpler tasks, existing tools are honestly pretty good at handling it. It is for these harder tasks where LLMs can fail
- A primary innovation of Zoro it’s is interface of visualizing the process of the coding agent as it codes.
- 
- The input is a task
- The output is a full plan breakdown of the task, showing if each step of the plan was completed, and if each rule was actually followed or not.
